Brayden Maynard (centre) goes to ground after being hit by Gold Coast player Ben Long. (Getty Images: Chris Hyde)

Collingwood defender Brayden Maynard could be in trouble after making contact with an umpire during a melee in the Magpies' six-point win over Gold Coast on Saturday.

Maynard rushed to Gold Coast's Ben Long, who in a previous melee moments earlier had hit the Collingwood defender in the ribs with a shoulder.

Maynard was left on the ground after that hit, and at half-time rushed to confront Long.

As players rushed towards the melee, Maynard's hands made brief contact with an umpire.

Suns midfielder Touk Miller, who also rushed into the melee, appeared to have made some sort of contact with the umpire after Maynard.

Maynard's contact, if deemed intentional, could result in a stint on the sideline.

Former AFL umpire Ray Chamberlain said the Magpie's vice-captain will have a difficult time justifying his actions if he is sent to the AFL Tribunal.

"He has no care for anything else except for his own want and need," Chamberlain told ABC Sport.

"He runs 30 metres to go after Ben Long and makes contact with an umpire in the process.

"He's going to have a lot of trouble explaining why that's OK."

GWS Giant Toby Green was suspended for six AFL matches after shoving an umpire in an elimination final in 2021.

Collingwood coach Craig McCrae said during his post-match press conference that he had not seen the footage of Maynard making contact with the umpire, but said he was not pleased with his star defender getting hit by Long.

"I'm not sure what the AFL do with that. I'm sure they'll be looking at it all," McCrae said of the melee.

"I wasn't happy with a guy getting hit off the ball. I'm not sure that's something we'd love every week."

Long may also have a nervous wait to see if he will be punished for his hit on Maynard, which started the sequence of events.

Speaking to Fox after the match, Maynard said he believed he may have suffered a broken rib from Long's hit.

"If you're going to come and hit me cheaply, you're going to get something back," Maynard said

"It's all part of the game. I didn't mind it really. I think I might have a broken rib, but it's all part of footy. We move on."

Meanwhile, Carlton has survived a late Richmond comeback to record its seventh consecutive win.

The Blues provisionally moved into the AFL's top 10 with a 10.14 (74) to10.12 (72) victory, after the Tigers kicked two goals in the final two minutes to set up a thrilling finish.

Fremantle's 14-match winning streak was snapped in Canberra after the GWS Giants rose to a 16.13 (109) to 13.10 (88) victory.

Jake Stringer kicked a career-high seven goals for the Giants in the 21-point upset.

Melbourne held off an enormous Hawthorn comeback to win 19.11 (125) to 14.6 (90) in Tasmania.

The Demons led by 96 points during the third quarter before the Hawks kicked 12 consecutive goals to threaten the greatest comeback in AFL history.

By Michael Doyle

An entertaining day of footy has come to an end.

We hope you join us then.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 10:44pm

By Michael Doyle

Carlton's stunning resurgence under Josh Fraser has yielded a seventh straight win, the Blues hanging on for a scrappy two-point victory over Richmond at the MCG.

Trailing by 18 points at quarter-time, Carlton put through eight of the next nine goals to set up their 10.14 (74) to 10.12 (72) win in front of 54,923 fans on a wet Saturday night.

Seemingly cruising when they led by 14 points with less than three minutes left, Richmond were the beneficiaries of two free kicks in front of goals.

The Tigers won the next centre clearance and had the ball inside their forward-50 in the dying seconds, but Carlton desperately hung on.

Staring at a wasted year when Michael Voss was sacked, the Blues have squared the ledger at 8-8 and jumped from 16th to 10th under their unassuming interim coach.

Under the newly introduced wildcard round, Carlton are currently in a finals position that seemed totally out of reach two months ago.

The Blues now face a defining month of games against Hawthorn, Collingwood, Gold Coast and Brisbane that will decide whether they progress to the post-season.

Carlton had to endure some nervous moments in the last quarter when the lead was cut to nine points, but held their nerve against the young Tigers to avoid an upset.

Rugged midfielder George Hewett, who was dropped during Voss's finals weeks as coach, slotted the match-winning goal to cap off a best-on-ground performance.

Rising Star favourite Jagga Smith was superb with a game-high 29 possessions, earning the praise of former Port Adelaide coach Ken Hinkley.

In radio commentary, Hinkley compared him to in-demand Power superstar Zak Butters.

In a match that didn't reach any great heights, tensions boiled over on quarter-time after a heated exchange between Blues ace Sam Walsh and Tigers youngster Jasper Alger.

The normally level-headed Walsh ran to push Alger over, giving away a free kick.

Alger booted the goal to give Richmond their best first quarter (5.3) of the season.

Nearly all players converged into the melee, forcing a late entry into their respective huddles.

Veteran forward Tom Lynch had a forgettable night, failing to redeem himself from the corresponding game earlier in the season when he kicked 2.7 in a close loss to the Blues.

Lynch sprayed his first set shot of the game, then kicked his two other shots on goal out on the full, stranding him on 499 career goals.

Richmond lost Jack Ross to concussion in the second quarter, the midfielder's second head knock in a month.

Already without Jacob Weitering and Harry Dean, Carlton were also dealt a blow when Lewis Young was ruled out with concussion in the second term.

That got way too close for comfort, if you're a Blues fan.

But Carlton held on and has seven consecutive wins.

George Hewett was terrific tonight with two goals and 26 touches.

He has just spoken to Fox Footy.

I think when we play Richmond, you can lock it in for a one-goal game. They match up really well against us. They played brilliant footy. Their effort was there; ours was there too.

Carlton has recorded a seventh-straight victory with a xx-point win over Richmond.

George Hewett led the way for the Blues with 26 touches and two goals.

The Tigers came so close to snatching victory late, with two goals in the final two minutes.

The ball was camped in Carlton's defensive 50 for the final minute of the match, but the Tigers could not fire a shot at goal.

Seth Campbell is hit high inside the forward 50 and had a set shot from in front.

He kicks the goal.

Blues only lead by 2 with 56 seconds to play.

Mykelti Lefau has kicked a goal for the Tigers, after the Blues were called for a deliberate rush behind, which was illegal.

By Michael Doyle

It has not been a happy return for Tom Lynch.

He has a set shot with 2:20 left in the match. He must kick it to keep Richmond's slim chances alive.

For the second time in this half, he misses everything.

By Michael Doyle

Carlton has managed the time very well.

With four minutes left, they have a 15-point advantage.

Richmond are fighting hard, but they cannot find the final kick to get the points they need.

By Michael Doyle

Excellent from George Hewett, when his team needed him.

He was ruled to have been hit high inside the forward 50 when diving for a ball on the ground.

With the set shot, he nails the long kick.

Blues by 15 with 8 minutes to play.

By Michael Doyle

It is the Tigers who have the first goal of the final term.

Taj Hotton charged onto a loose ball that was tapped down from a ball-up.

He was not steady as he ran through the pack, threw the footy on the boot, and kicked the goal.

Blues by 9.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:50pm

By Michael Doyle

Carlton's Talor Byrne took a nice mark near the top of the 50-metre arc.

But his set shot just fades through for a behind.

Blues lead by 15 with 12 minutes to play.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:47pm

By Michael Doyle

We don't have a goal, yet.

But we do have tension.

The ball has been hotly contested since the start of the final term.

Each side has a pair of behinds.

Blues by 14.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:32pm

By Michael Doyle

Carlton has the lead, but Richmond is in this contest.

The Tigers missed a few set shots in that quarter, which they may come to rue.

The Blues are playing well, but they cannot turn their foot off the gas in the final term.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:21pm

By Michael Doyle

It is a quick response for the Tigers.

A nice clearance leads to an uncontested mark inside forward 50 for Rhyan Mansell.

The Tiger makes no error with the set shot.

Blues by 13.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:20pm

By Michael Doyle

Carlton kicks long into the forward 50 where Harry McKay leaps for a mark.

Everyone on the field stops. Why? Everyone is waiting for the umpire to call a free kick after McKay had his arms chopped.

The whistle never came, and Carlton's Brodie Kemp was tackled with the ball.

A ball-up is called. Ball up? If the play was still going, why was Kemp not penalised for holding the ball?

From the ball-up, George Hewett gets the ball and kicks the goal.

For anyone new to our country and wants to learn this wonderful game, best of luck.

Blues by 19.

Sat 4 Jul 2026 at 9:11pm

By Michael Doyle

Very nice from Carlton.

After an interception inside the forward half,  Harry McKay took a mark and then kicked the goal.

The Blues lead by 14.

Tom Lynch has missed a set shot early in the third quarter for the Tigers.

It is going to be tough footy for the next phase of this match.
